Rhode Island Red.description: American breed known for reliable egg production and hardiness. Medium-sized birds with deep red plumage and red-brown eyes.
Rhode Island Red.cold_hardiness: Excellent — large comb can be susceptible to frostbite, but otherwise very hardy

Speckled Sussex.description: British breed with distinctive mahogany and white speckled plumage. Curious, active foragers with excellent table manners (quiet compared to other breeds).
Speckled Sussex.temperament: Docile, curious, excellent foragers, friendly to humans
Speckled Sussex.cold_hardiness: Good — medium comb, adapts well to cold

Golden Laced Wyandotte.description: American breed with beautiful gold and black laced plumage. Compact, muscular birds with rose combs (frost-resistant) and yellow legs.
Golden Laced Wyandotte.temperament: Hardy, independent, can be broody, broody hens are excellent mothers
Golden Laced Wyandotte.cold_hardiness: Excellent — rose comb is frost-resistant, compact body, ideal for cold climates

Easter Egger.description: Not a standard breed but a hybrid type that lays colored eggs (blue, green, or pink). Variable plumage; typically have ear tufts or muffs and beards.

White Rock.description: American breed with white plumage and yellow legs. Large, friendly birds originally bred for meat production. Commonly crossed with other breeds.
White Rock.temperament: Friendly, calm, excellent mothers (when broody), good foragers
White Rock.cold_hardiness: Good — large comb can be susceptible to frostbite

Black Australorp.description: Australian breed with glossy black plumage with a green sheen. Medium-sized, docile birds known for excellent egg production.
Black Australorp.temperament: Docile, friendly, good mothers (broody), excellent foragers
Black Australorp.cold_hardiness: Good — moderate comb, handles cold well

Easter Egger \u00d7 Rhode Island Red Cro.description: Hybrid offspring combining Easter Egger's colored-egg genetics with RIR vigor. Inherits blue-egg production from EE parent and reliability from RIR.
Easter Egger \u00d7 Rhode Island Red Cro.temperament: Friendly, curious, good foragers, benefits from hybrid vigor

White Broad-Breasted Turkey.description: The standard commercial turkey breed. Fast-growing, broad-chested birds raised primarily for meat. White plumage makes for clean processing.
White Broad-Breasted Turkey.temperament: Curious, social, can imprint on handlers when raised from poults
White Broad-Breasted Turkey.cold_hardiness: Moderate — need shelter from wind and wet, but tolerate cold if dry

Brahma.description: Large, heavily feathered breed known as the 'King of Chickens.' Broad body, feathered feet, pea comb. Originally bred for meat but makes a calm dual-purpose bird.
Brahma.temperament: Calm, docile, cold-hardy, slow to mature
Brahma.cold_hardiness: Excellent — pea comb resists frostbite, heavy feathering insulates well, bred for northern climates

Bronze Broad-Breasted Turkey.description: Large commercial turkey breed with iridescent bronze plumage. Heavier and darker than the White Broad-Breasted variety; raised primarily for meat with striking traditional appearance.
Bronze Broad-Breasted Turkey.temperament: Curious, social, can imprint on handlers when raised from poults
Bronze Broad-Breasted Turkey.cold_hardiness: Moderate — need shelter from wind and wet, but tolerate cold if dry

Barred Plymouth Rock.description: American breed with distinctive black-and-white horizontal barring. Hardy dual-purpose chicken, friendly and reliable layer of brown eggs.
Barred Plymouth Rock.temperament: Calm, friendly, good foragers, tolerant of confinement
Barred Plymouth Rock.cold_hardiness: Excellent — handles cold New England winters well

Plymouth Rock (variety TBD).description: American Plymouth Rock breed, exact variety to be confirmed as the chicks feather out. Plymouth Rock varieties include Barred, White, Buff, Silver Penciled, Partridge, Columbian, Blue, and Speckled (Mottled).
Plymouth Rock (variety TBD).temperament: Calm, friendly, good foragers, tolerant of confinement
Plymouth Rock (variety TBD).cold_hardiness: Excellent — handles cold New England winters well

Cream Legbar.description: British autosexing breed developed in the 1930s by crossing Brown Leghorns, Barred Plymouth Rocks, and Araucanas. Crested with a distinctive head tuft. Known for blue/green eggs and chicks that can be sexed by down pattern at hatch.
Cream Legbar.temperament: Active, alert, good foragers, friendly but flighty
Cream Legbar.cold_hardiness: Good — moderate single comb, copes with cold if dry

Blue Laced Red Wyandotte.description: Wyandotte variety with deep red ground color and blue (slate-gray) lacing on each feather. Same compact rose-comb body as the Golden and Silver Laced Wyandottes — bred for cold climates and reliable winter laying.
Blue Laced Red Wyandotte.temperament: Hardy, independent, calm, can go broody
Blue Laced Red Wyandotte.cold_hardiness: Excellent — rose comb resists frostbite, compact muscular body

Buff Ranger.description: Buff/golden free-range meat hybrid — a 'Ranger'-type broiler in the Freedom/Red Ranger family. Heavy-bodied, fast-growing, and an active forager, bred for pasture-raised meat as a slower-growing, hardier alternative to the industrial Cornish Cross.
Buff Ranger.egg_color: Brown (if kept on to lay; primarily a meat bird, not a production layer)
Buff Ranger.eggs_per_year: 150-200 (kept hens only; not bred for laying)
Buff Ranger.temperament: Active, robust, voracious foragers — Boss calls them 'monstrous little eating machines'
Buff Ranger.cold_hardiness: Good — hardy hybrid, but the heavy meat frame needs clean dry bedding and benefits from shelter
Buff Ranger.typical_lifespan: Bred for meat; can live several years as pets, though the heavy frame strains legs and heart over time

Bantam (breed TBD).description: Bantam is a size class, not a single breed — a miniature chicken, typically a quarter to a third the size of a standard fowl. The farm's bantams trace to the Cackle Hatchery exotic/rare assortment (08-April-2026 arrival), so exact breeds are still resolving as they feather out. Possible bantam types in that batch include Cubalaya, Phoenix, Sumatra, Yokohama, Cochin, and Polish.
Bantam (breed TBD).eggs_per_year: Varies — generally fewer and smaller than standard fowl (often 100-180)
Bantam (breed TBD).temperament: Varies by breed — often active, alert, characterful; many are good flyers and tight broodies
Bantam (breed TBD).cold_hardiness: Varies — small bodies lose heat faster, so reliable dry shelter matters in New England winters

Polish (bantam).description: Crested ornamental breed, instantly recognized by the big rounded pouf of feathers on the head, which grows from a bony knob on the skull. Comes in standard and bantam sizes; the farm's is a bantam. Plumage varieties include White-Crested Black/Blue, Silver/Golden Laced, and Splash. More of a show-and-pet bird than a production layer.
Polish (bantam).eggs_per_year: 150-200 (small white eggs; not a heavy layer)
Polish (bantam).temperament: Docile and people-friendly, but can be flighty or startle easily because the crest blocks their vision
Polish (bantam).cold_hardiness: Fair — the crest soaks up water and can freeze, so dry shelter matters; the small comb is low frostbite risk, but a wet crest is the real cold-weather concern
